Title: 10 missing after avalanche hits Nepal's Himlung peak base camp
Article:
KATHMANDU: At least 10 local climbers and guides are missing after an avalanche hit the base camp of Himlung peak in central Nepal early Sunday, an expedition organiser said.
The Himalayan country is already reeling from a devastating, tsunami-like flood on August 26 that killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 missing.
The 7,126-metre tall Himlung peak, located near the border with Tibet, had several days of heavy snowfall ahead of the avalanche.
Two helicopters and a search and rescue team are on standby but have not been able to move because of adverse weather, Bibhuti Chand Thakur of Himalaya Holidays Trekking told AFP.
"Eight members of our expedition team and two more from another company have been reported missing," Thakur said, adding that all those missing are Nepali.
Nepal is home to eight of the world's 14 highest peaks and foreign climbers who flock to its mountains are a major source of revenue for the largely rural country.
Nepal has issued more than 500 permits for the autumn climbing season, with the world's eighth highest mountain Manaslu accounting for most of them.
Heavy snowfall on Manaslu this week forced climbers to cancel expeditions.
Treks were also paused to the Dhaulagiri mountain range.
Parts of Nepal have also seen heavy rainfall since Thursday which has washed away roads and triggered landslides.--AFP

Title: Heavy rain kills 56 in India's Uttar Pradesh
Article:
LUCKNOW: Heavy rain triggered floods and landslides in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh, killing at least 56 people over the past three days, a government disaster agency said on Sunday.
Uttar Pradesh, India's most populous state with more than 240 million people, is frequently battered by rain and thunderstorms during the annual monsoon season from June to September.
The latest deaths were reported during a spell of "exceptionally heavy rain that has affected much of Uttar Pradesh", the Relief Commissioner's office said in a statement.
More than 1,000 houses were damaged after "a depression over the Bay of Bengal moved inland and intensified rainfall across the region", it said.
India's weather office has warned in recent years of an increase in extreme weather events, including intense thunderstorms and lightning, which experts link to rising temperatures and changing climate patterns.
The statement said the state recorded 66.5 millimetres of rain between Friday and Sunday, compared to the season average of 7.6 millimetres. --AFP

Title: Bangkok floods: Malaysians advised to register with e-Konsular
Article:
BANGKOK: Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to remain in contact with the Malaysian Embassy for assistance and updates following extensive flooding that affected several districts and major transportation routes in the capital city.
The Foreign Ministry, in an advisory on Sunday, said several Malaysians had been affected by the floods, and that the Embassy in
Bangkok
was extending necessary support and assistance to them.
It said Malaysians requiring consular assistance, or those with information on other Malaysians who may be affected by the floods, can contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Bangkok at +66 2 340 5720, +66 2 340 5731 or +66 87 028 4659, or email mwbangkok@kln.gov.my.
It strongly urged Malaysians who had yet to do so to register their presence in Thailand via the e-Konsular system.
"The embassy remains in close communication with local authorities as it continues to monitor the situation," it said.
The ministry also advised Malaysians residing in or visiting Bangkok to exercise caution, remain vigilant and strictly follow safety directives issued by the local authorities.
"Malaysians travelling to Suvarnabhumi Airport are also advised to allow additional travel time and arrive well ahead of their scheduled departure, as access routes may experience delays," it said.
Persistent heavy rain since Thursday had caused flooding across all 50 districts of Bangkok.

Title: MCMC blocked 101.66 million spoof calls from Feb to Aug
Article:
KULAI:The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with telecommunications service providers, blocked a total of 101.66 million scam or spoof calls from Feb to Aug.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said this was achieved through the implementation of the Inter Operator Spoofing Gateway initiative, which has been in place since the beginning of this year.
She said that scammers from abroad use Caller ID Spoofing tactics to display phone numbers as if they are from local telco networks to deceive victims in this country.
"The total number of spoof calls blocked, amounting to 101.66 million, proves that this initiative is very effective," she told reporters when met at the Watch a Movie with the Kulai MP programme here.
She said this when asked to comment on the number of scam calls blocked so far.
Meanwhile, Teo said the MCMC will hold an online meeting with Meta tomorrow regarding public complaints concerning blocked WhatsApp accounts.
She said the meeting was to obtain a detailed briefing regarding the case.
"We (the ministry) will wait for the results (information) from the meeting on that day," she said.
MCMC had previously reported that it was investigating public complaints regarding WhatsApp accounts that were reported to have been hacked, blocked, or no longer accessible.
The commission also said that it has submitted the case to Meta for clarification and appropriate action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families of 55 missing in Nepal seek Anwar's help over death declaration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Families of 55 Malaysians still missing in Nepal want Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to intervene in securing an expedited declaration of death.
They say they cannot afford to remain in legal and financial limbo for the seven-year period under existing procedures.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families were seeking a special exception for the 55 Malaysians, given the scale and circumstances of the disaster.
He said they wanted the matter resolved through a government-to-government (G2G) mechanism between Malaysia and Nepal, rather than leaving individual families to navigate lengthy legal proceedings.
Earlier, Dr Manivannan said the families faced a seven-year wait before a death declaration can be produced.
He said the families wanted the government to examine whether an exception could be made for the 55 Malaysians, allowing the death declaration to be issued much sooner so that their families could access insurance, compensation, bank funds and inheritance.
Dr Manivannan said the families could explore other legal avenues, such as bringing the issue to the courts.
However, he asked for legal assistance as the families could not realistically sustain court proceedings that could take years.
He said the families also wanted temporary relief from financial commitments linked to the missing people while waiting for the legal process to be resolved.
"What we ask for is a moratorium for 55 people who are missing," he said.
Dr Manivannan said the government could provide such assistance without waiting for Nepal to complete its own processes.
"We don't even need to wait for the government of Nepal. There are a lot of things that we can do in Malaysia now," he said.
He said the families wanted to meet Anwar as soon as possible.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Diversification, regional resilience will ensure Malacca Strait relevance
Article:
LETTER:
Global trade is entering a new phase as a shipping corridor through the Arctic Ocean, which is known as the Northern Sea Route (NSR), promoted as a quicker alternative to the traditional maritime transit through Suez.
Although NSR is risky as it cuts through icy waters, it can save the voyage duration between Asia and Europe by approximately 30 to 45 per cent which is equivalent to around 10 to 14 days depending on the specific sailing route and ports involved.
For China, the NSR not only provides a shorter distance but lower fuel costs resulting in faster delivery and reduce dependency on other congested strategic waterways.
However, it can only be navigable between July and October when ice melts enough. To allow safe passage for ships, assistance from ice-class hulls and icebreaker escorts is needed, which can add to the costs.
Due to the high-risk zone of the Arctic, insurance premiums are higher. At the same time, Russia, which controls the NSR, also charges navigation and pilotage fees.
These hidden costs often cancel out the savings from shorter distance.
Only on this route, the volume of Russian-Chinese cargo in 2025 amounted to 5.4 million tonnes, while the total cargo turnover of the NSR is approaching 40 million tonnes in 2026, evidence that the NSR is not an experiment anymore.
South Korea this year has launched its first commercial voyage to the Arctic with the container ship PanStar Acro leaving Busan in August and calling at Felixstowe, Rotterdam and Gdansk, putting Busan on the map as a maritime hub for future Arctic trade.
European ports including Rotterdam, Hamburg and Gdansk are bracing for more arrivals from the Arctic. This is a development we should pay close attention.
Our ports such as Port Klang, Penang, Johor Port (Pasir Gudang), and Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) rely heavily on the Asia-Europe trade through the Strait of Malacca and the Suez Canal.
If more cargo bypasses these waters during summer, even temporarily, it would cut transshipment volumes. Port fees, logistics services and related industries may feel the impact.
The Strait of Malacca carries about a quarter of global trade. Port Klang has thrived as a hub because of this. But the rise of the Arctic route, even as an occasional option, shows trade is diversifying. Malaysia cannot ignore this shift.
The Suez Canal remains dominant, open year-round, reliable, and backed by strong infrastructure. The Arctic route is seasonal and risky, but China's investment in scheduled voyages signals a trend.
Climate change is also extending the Arctic's navigation window, making it more viable over time.
We must strategically plan ahead of time. Our ports should capture more intra-Asean trade and regional logistics, not rely only on Asia-Europe transshipment.
Investment in resilience, diversification, and cooperation with Asean partners will keep Malaysia strong in global shipping.
In brief, the Arctic route is shorter but not always cheaper. It is seasonal, risky, and controlled by Russia.
Yet its growth signals change in global trade. Even small diversions can ripple through our economy.
We should act now by diversify port strategies and strengthen regional ties to protect the importance of the Strait of Malacca.
ASSOC PROFESSOR DR HASNIZA MOHD TAIB
Senior Lecturer
School of Economics Finance and Banking
Universiti Utara Malaysia
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor haze likely linked to smoke from southern Sumatra
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Smoke from fires in Indonesia's southern Sumatra is believed to be contributing to the haze blanketing Johor, with prevailing winds carrying transboundary smoke across the Malacca Strait into southern Peninsular Malaysia.
The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported that moderate to dense smoke plumes were observed emanating from hotspot clusters in southern Sumatra, while haze from the region had also been observed moving towards Singapore and southern Peninsular Malaysia.
The pattern suggests the haze has shifted towards southern Peninsular Malaysia, with transboundary smoke from southern Sumatra a likely contributor.
ASMC serves as the regional centre for weather, climate and haze monitoring. It assesses the risk of transboundary haze based on factors including hotspot activity, smoke density, rainfall and prevailing wind patterns.
Heavy rain across parts of Johor today brought a slight improvement in air quality, with
Air Pollutant Index (API)
readings easing at several monitoring stations.
Earlier this morning, four Johor monitoring stations recorded the country's highest API readings with Kota Tinggi at 165, Pasir Gudang at 164, Pengerang at 162 and Larkin at 156.
As of 4pm, four of Johor's eight air-quality monitoring stations registered 'unhealthy' readings, led by Pasir Gudang with an API reading of 161.
Kota Tinggi recorded 159, followed by Pengerang (158) and Larkin (152), while Tangkak, Batu Pahat and Kluang remained in the moderate category at 62, 72 and 68, respectively.
Segamat recorded a good API reading of 58.
Meanwhile, Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) also reported yesterday that smoke plumes were observed emanating from fires in southern Sumatra, while prevailing winds were forecast to blow from the southeast or southwest.
Last month, Malaysian Meteorological Department Director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the haze was expected to persist as long as open fires continued in Sumatra and Kalimantan during the Southwest Monsoon.
He was quoted as saying that smoke from fires in Sumatra is contributing to the haze, with the Southwest Monsoon winds consistently carrying smoke from Indonesia towards Malaysia.

Title: School must be a place of safety, not fear
Article:
LETTERS:
The death of a 14-year-old student at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah is deeply distressing and should remind us all that violence should not be condoned or tolerated in any educational institution.
While police investigations are still ongoing and the exact cause of death has yet to be established, the fact that a 16-year-old student has been detained in connection with the case makes it imperative that we take the issue of violence among students extremely seriously.
We have spoken repeatedly about bullying and violence in schools. But if such incidents continue to occur, we must ask whether our existing preventive measures are working effectively.
We cannot wait for more such tragedies to occur.
I urge the Education Ministry and schools to strengthen preventive measures, particularly in hostels:
•
Strengthen supervision, especially during after-school and night-time hours.
•
Establish an effective early-warning system so that bullying, threats and violent behaviour are detected before they escalate.
•
Make it easier and safer for students to report bullying confidentially, without fear of retaliation.
•
Ensure every serious allegation of bullying or violence is promptly investigated and not dismissed as merely a disciplinary matter.
• Strengthen counselling and psychological support for victims, witnesses and students who display aggressive behaviour.
• Train teachers, wardens and school administrators to recognise early signs of bullying, intimidation and violent behaviour.
Most importantly, we must create a culture where students speak up, teachers listen and schools act.
Every child has the right to learn and live in a school environment free from fear, intimidation and violence.
A school is not safe simply because there are rules on paper. It is safe when those rules are actively enforced and every warning sign is taken seriously.
The immediate investigation must establish the facts and ensure justice for the family. At the same time, let this tragedy strengthen our resolve to prevent another young life from being lost to violence.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
SAFETY ADVOCATE
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Families face 7-year wait for death declaration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The families of 55 Malaysians still missing following the disaster in Nepal are facing a seven-year wait before they can seek a declaration of death, leaving them in prolonged legal and financial limbo.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the National Registration Department told the families that the Nepalese government would first have to make a declaration, followed by a statement from the Nepalese embassy.
"Only then can the heir ask the NRD for a declaration of death. The second point is, the heir can ask for a declaration of death after seven years.
"A police report has to have been made, and the heir has to wait for seven years," he told reporters after a meeting with government agencies at the Foreign Ministry today.
Dr Manivannan said the wait could have serious financial consequences for families already struggling to meet commitments.
"Even now, the heirs would have been in financial trouble for a month or two. In six years, I think everyone will have no home, no car... so, that's a big issue," he said.
He said the families wanted the government to explore an exceptional legal mechanism, given the scale of the Nepal disaster.
"This is not a disaster where one or two people are missing. Thousands of people have gone missing, or died," he said.
Dr Manivannan said the families were prepared to pursue the matter collectively through the courts but needed the necessary documentation from Nepal.
"We need someone high up, like the prime minister... the government needs to help us now, not later. And this is really urgent."
Earlier, Dr Manivannan told reporters the DNA samples taken from family members of the 55 missing Malaysians had
yet to be processed
.

Title: Global South must have greater say in AI-goverance - Mohamad Hasan
Article:
NEW YORK: The Global South must have a meaningful role in shaping decisions on artificial intelligence (AI) rather than merely becoming a destination for data centres, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said AI was transforming economies, societies and government decision-making, thus creating enormous opportunities but also significant risks.
"The Global South cannot simply become a destination for data centres, while decisions about AI are made elsewhere," he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Saturday.
Mohamad said the UN must continue empowering Global South countries, which are likely to be more greatly affected by inequitable AI development, to participate in global discussions on AI.
"We must be partners in innovation. Not merely customers and markets. And not merely destinations for investment," he said.
He said equitable decision-making and equitable development were necessary to ensure that the benefits of AI could be shared more broadly across borders.
Mohamad also called for the enormous demands that technology infrastructure places on water, energy, land and other resources to be managed.
"Technology must serve humanity. Never the reverse," he said.
He said the answer could not be for a small number of companies or countries to decide the rules for everyone else.
The Global South comprises 134 countries, representing about 80 per cent of the world's population, according to the UN.
Mohamad is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 for Malaysia's participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal disaster: SMART did not search Rasuwagadhi due to operational constraints
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) did not conduct a direct search for survivors and victims at Rasuwagadhi, the site of a catastrophic avalanche and flash flood in Nepal, due to operational constraints and lack of approval.
This was conveyed by SMART commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa to families of the 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable in Nepal, during a briefing at Wisma Putra today.
Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said the families had sought an explanation on why SMART did not search the Rasuwagadhi area, which was among locations believed to be relevant to the missing Malaysians.
He said Abdul Manaf had detailed the operational limitations faced by the team and that the search was conducted in areas that could be safely accessed and approved by Nepalese authorities.
SMART's deployment in Nepal previously included ground searches and drone surveillance in Rasuwa.
[[nid:1542327]]
Dr Manivannan said the families were also told that while the possibility of survival had not been ruled out, the chances were now "very slim" after 33 days.
Nepal is expected to end the search-and-rescue (SAR) phase soon and move towards recovery, verification and rebuilding, he said.
"The possibility of survival has not been ruled out, but the chances are very slim after 33 days," Dr Manivannan told reporters after the briefing.
He said the families' focus was now also on identifying any remains recovered from the disaster.
On DNA matching, Dr Manivannan said all 101 samples from the Malaysian families had been processed in Malaysia, with three already sent to China after immigration records confirmed the three Malaysians had crossed into China.
The remaining 98 samples had also been processed, and their results would be uploaded to a designated system for comparison with DNA obtained from victims and remains recovered in Nepal.
However, he said Nepal has yet to start processing the DNA samples.
Dr Manivannan said he had asked for all 101 samples to also be shared with China as a precaution.
"We don't want to take any chances," he said.
He said any unidentified remains recovered in Nepal would be tagged and buried, allowing families to claim them later if DNA matching established their identities.
"If there is a match in DNA later, then the families may come and claim the remains," he said.
The SMART team, comprising 11 personnel, was deployed to Nepal on Sept 5 with 12.4 tonnes of equipment, including drones, and returned on Sept 14 after conducting searches in areas deemed safe and approved by Nepalese authorities.
The Foreign Ministry has said SMART's return did not mean efforts to establish the status of the 55 Malaysians had ended, with Nepalese authorities continuing search, verification and identification efforts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thousands seek to thwart disputed N.Ireland flashpoint parade
Article:
PORTADOWN: Thousands gathered Sunday in a Northern Irish town seeking to halt a contentious pro-British Protestant march from passing through a mainly Catholic and nationalist area for the first time in 28 years.
The tensions spiked after a court in the early hours of Sunday cleared the march by the Orange Order to go ahead.
The Parades Commission, Northern Ireland's independent body regulating contentious processions, had authorised 35 Orangemen to march silently along Garvaghy Road in Portadown, without bands or supporters from 8am (0700 GMT) Sunday.
Northern Ireland was blighted for three decades by conflict between largely Catholic, pro-Irish republicans and Protestant, pro-UK unionists, and the Garvaghy Road became a major flashpoint during the late 1990s.
About 2,000 people walked early Sunday in the Garvaghy Road area of Portadown, 25 miles southwest of Belfast, in a counter-protest seeking to prevent the Orange march.
There was a heavy security presence, and police held up the Orange Order rally inside a church hall, an AFP correspondent saw.
Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, of the Irish republican Sinn Fein party, condemned the late-night court ruling allowing the march to go ahead.
"Our message tonight is clear. There is no going back. Not tomorrow. Not ever," said O'Neill.
She said she supported "the right of the Garvaghy Road residents to protest against this unwanted sectarian march."
Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald told reporters as she walked with the counter-protesters that the "residents and community have come out to defend their right to live free from sectarian harassment."
Since the 1998 Good Friday peace accords ending the so-called Troubles in Northern Ireland "there has been lots of progress ... it has been transformational. People's lives have been changed fundamentally," she said, adding "we are not going back."
[[nid:1542322]]
The procession had survived a series of last-minute legal challenges.
A Belfast High Court judge temporarily blocked it on Saturday, warning that the long-running dispute could escalate across Northern Ireland and urging the parties to "step back from the abyss."
But shortly before midnight, a three-judge Court of Appeal panel overturned the injunction, ruling that the judge had "erred in law."
The substantive legal challenge was returned to the High Court, but the appeal decision left the procession free to begin at 8am (0700 GMT) on Sunday.
Carla Lockhart, a local MP from the pro-British Democratic Unionist Party, called the appeal overturn "seismic" and said residents had nothing to fear.
"Thirty-five men walking down a road silently with no bands in an orderly fashion; there is nothing to fear," she said.
The confrontation, known as the Drumcree dispute after the church attended by the marchers, became a major flashpoint during the late 1990s.
Attempts to force the parade through, or prevent it from proceeding, repeatedly triggered serious disorder.
The Parades Commission was established in 1998, the year the Good Friday Agreement largely ended three decades of conflict over British rule known as the Troubles.
It barred the Order from completing the route that year and has consistently rejected subsequent applications.
The issue was revived in August when the High Court quashed the commission's latest restriction because of procedural failings, without ruling that the Order had a right to march along Garvaghy Road.
The Order then submitted a fresh application, leading to Friday's decision permitting the restricted procession.
The Orange Order is an pro-British organisation that takes its name from William of Orange, the Protestant Dutchman who seized the English, Scottish and Ireland throne from Catholic King James II in 1689.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: DNA samples from families of Malaysians yet to be processed, says group
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: DNA samples provided by families of 55 Malaysians still missing in Nepal have yet to be processed, according to Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam.
"So far, they haven't processed even one yet. That's what we understand. So far, they're just taking the DNA, but it hasn't been processed," he told reporters after a meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today.
Dr Manivannan said 98 DNA samples had been provided to Nepal, while three were given to China in a different format requested by its authorities.
He said the samples were collected in preparation for comparison with DNA extracted from any remains recovered in Nepal.
"What will happen after this, both these, they will match," he said, explaining that the samples from families and recovered remains would be processed and compared.
He said the families had also been told that recovered remains would be tagged and could be exhumed if a DNA match was established.
"If there is DNA matching, let's say the family member of one or two of them has a matching, we can go to Nepal and get the body, they will dig it," he said.
However, he said the families wanted official confirmation of the process.
"But officially, we do not accept any claims," he said.

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast in 7 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in parts of seven states until 7pm today.
In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement.
The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Kapit, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Bintulu, Miri, Limbang, Samarahan, Serian, Kuching and Sri Aman (Lubok Antu).
In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast (Ranau, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Kota Belud, Penampang and Papar), Interior (Keningau, Tambunan, Pensiangan, Sook, Tenom, Sipitang, Beaufort and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Sandakan).

Title: Armizan hopes for more Rahmah sales allocation in 2027 Budget
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali hopes that the allocation for Madani Rahmah Sales Programme (Jualan Rahmah) can be increased in the 2027 Budget to allow the programme to be further expanded and benefit more people.
He said the encouraging response and the savings enjoyed by the public form the basis of the government's commitment to continue and expand the implementation of the programme as one of the interventions to address the cost of living issue.
"Therefore, we hope and appeal to the Finance Ministry, in particular, to consider increasing the allocation in the 2027 Budget, as this is a programme that directly reaches the people, allowing them to benefit from the subsidy in a targeted and direct manner on the ground," he said.
He said this at the 'Majlis Selawat dan Tadabbur Syukbah' organised by the Papar Parliamentary Women's Wing at the Papar District Mosque today, which was attended by approximately 1,500 people.
Armizan said that with the specific allocation established starting from the 2024 Budget, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has been able to set annual and monthly implementation targets and expand public access to Rahmah Sales.
He added that from January 2023 to Sept 23, 2026, Rahmah Sales recorded a total of 81,455,623 transactions, with the figure showing a significant increase each year.
"Of that total, 9,244,504 transactions were recorded in 2023, rising to 12,826,708 transactions in 2024.
"With the increased allocation channeled to the ministry, public participation in Juala Rahmah rose significantly, reaching 27,534,770 transactions in 2025 and surging further to 31,849,641 transactions for the period of January 1 to September 23, 2026," he said.
He said the increase in transactions reflects the public's positive response to Rahmah Sales, which offers daily necessities at prices 10 to 30 per cent lower than local market rates.
Armizan said the initiative was originally piloted as a government-led discount sales programme under the Payung RAHMAH agenda in 2023 before being strengthened into PJRM in 2024, thereby becoming a permanent government initiative with a dedicated allocation.
Meanwhile, Armizan said public access to information regarding Rahmah Sales events has also been improved in tandem with the expanded scale of the programme's implementation.
He said the public can now check the Rahmah Sales via PJRM website and Info Jualan Rahmah Madani app, which is available for download on Google Play Store and Apple App Store.
He said that starting Oct 1, the ministry is introducing special stickers displaying the Rahmah Sales schedule QR code at public hotspots nationwide.
"The installation of these special stickers is subject to the request and consent of the premises' management or owners. By scanning the QR code, the public can refer to the Rahmah schedule to check the dates and locations of events held near their respective areas.
"Locations where the stickers are being displayed include public housing areas, public markets, farmers' markets and tamu (traditional markets), halls and community centres, public transport terminals, places of worship, religious institutions, and business premises," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 132 Kemas preschools for children with autism to begin operation in January
Article:
MELAKA: A total of 132 Community Development Department (Kemas) preschools (Tabika) for children with autism will begin operations next January.
Its director-general, Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man, said the screening process for the admission of these special-needs children will open next month in collaboration with the Health Ministry.
"God willing, I believe this will benefit at least nearly 2,000 children with autism as the number of applications (from parents) is quite high.
"However, for the time being, we can only accommodate a maximum of 15 children per class specifically between 10 and 15 because each class will have three teachers... with one teacher supervising five to seven children, in accordance with established standards," he said.
He said this when met by reporters after the opening of the Melaka State Kemas Community Festival 2026 at Semabok Dalam Multipurpose Hall today.
The festival was officiated by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Mohammad Hanafiah said one of the prerequisites for attending these classes is possessing a Persons with Disabilities (PwD) card issued by the Welfare Department.
He added that this measure was taken to ensure alignment with policies set by the Education Ministry.
"If we look at the Education Ministry, children in these special classes receive an allowance as special-needs children.
"Therefore, we also want to ensure these special-needs children are registered with the Welfare Department so that they, too, can receive the allowance or assistance planned by the Education Ministry," he said.

Title: Perlis Raja Muda visits learning centre in MAIPs programme
Article:
KANGAR: Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail visited the Community Learning Centre (CLBC) in Kampung Seberang Ramai, Kuala Perlis yesterday, accompanied by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, as part of the Kayuhan MAIPs Peduli programme organised by the Perlis Islamic Religious and Malay Customs Council (MAIPs).
Perlis state secretary Datuk Noor Azman Abdul Rahman, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and MAIPs chief executive officer Mohd Nazim Mohd Noor were also part of the visit.
[[nid:1542302]]
Istana Arau, in a statement today, said that during the visit, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra observed an ongoing English tuition class involving students from the local community.
It said the students also took part in learning sessions and talks on bullying prevention, identifying false information and cybersecurity, providing children and students with early exposure to the importance of protecting themselves in the digital environment.
"The talk on Consumer Safety and the Integrity of the National Communications Network also emphasised the safe, ethical and responsible use of communications facilities, including being more vigilant against online scams, harmful content and cyber threats," it said.
[[nid:1542301]]
Istana Arau said the programme around the Royal Transformation Project at Kampung Nelayan Warna-Warni gave participants an opportunity to engage with the community and learn about its unique local identity and heritage.
It said Fahmi also took time to visit several interesting spots in the area, including Laman Congkak, Laman Bunga Kertas, Laman Laksa, Rumah Dodol and Jambatan Tuanku Syed Putra.
"During the same programme, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra, in his capacity as MAIPs president, also presented MAIPs contributions to three selected asnaf recipients in conjunction with the 68th edition of Kayuhan MAIPs Peduli this year.
[[nid:1542300]]
"The recipients were Idrus Remli, 62, from Taman Wai Permai; Salmiah Hamzah, 73, from Kampung Seberang Alor, Kuala Perlis; and Rusnani Khamis, 63, from Kampung Wai," Istana Arau said.
Kayuhan MAIPs Peduli is one of MAIPs' regular initiatives to engage directly with the community, while providing assistance to asnaf in need and promoting healthy lifestyles among the public.
The initiative reflects MAIPs' continued commitment to strengthening its outreach and engagement with communities, while ensuring the welfare of those in need remains a priority. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police declare major incident at UK's Fairford air base, used by US air forces
Article:
LONDON: British police said on Sunday they had arrested several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and the army was examining a number of vehicles after security was stepped up at a British air base used by US air forces in southwest England.
The British government gave authorisation to the US to use RAF Fairford to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that are attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
A Reuters eyewitness said armed police were blocking access to the main gate of the base. Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were stationed in the village of Fairford near the base.
"A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.
It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act," Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the air base.
"The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles."
A spokesperson for the US Air Force said they would not discuss specific force protection measures.
"The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said.
"We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families."
Britain said in July its armed forces were ​ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guards issued a warning not to allow US bombers to ‌fly from Fairford.
British ministers have also briefed providers of critical infrastructure of the threat posed by Russia, with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks.
Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration raids same-sex entertainment centre in KL
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department uncovered activities at an entertainment centre in the capital featuring dance performances by individuals of the same gender during a special operation early this morning.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said during the joint operation with the National Anti-Drug Agency, which began at 12.05am, three Chinese nationals and one Filipino national — all male and aged between 21 and 31 — were detained.
"All the foreign nationals were detained for suspected offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and were taken to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action.
"Three local men were issued notices to report to the office to assist with the investigation," he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said the entertainment centre, located on Jalan Klang Lama and operational since last year, is believed to have offered entertainment and dance performances by foreigners of the same gender, targeting both local and foreign customers in the Klang Valley.
"Charges ranged from RM53 to RM700, depending on the drinks ordered and table reservations made by customers," he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCBA: Cannabis smuggling attempts foiled 'almost daily' at Malaysian airports
Article:
SEGAMAT: Attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers out of Malaysia are being foiled almost daily at Kuala Lumpur International Airport, with foreigners making up most of those detained, the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) said today.
Director Datuk Sri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the agency had stepped up targeted screening at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2 following a recent incident involving a Malaysian pilot who was detained in Indonesia.
In July, the
pilot was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport
in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg into the country. Indonesian authorities also seized 2.74g of methamphetamine and a further 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue.
Suhaily said almost every day, or at least every week, MCBA detained those attempting to smuggle cannabis flowers out of the country.
"Most are not Malaysians but foreigners," he told a press conference after the MCBA Basic Officer Training Course Series 1/2026 closing ceremony held at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) here today.
He said MCBA was tasked with coordinating screening with Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) at both KLIA terminals.
MCBA was also given three key responsibilities at international airports under 17 government initiatives to strengthen border security.
"The three main areas are coordinating targeted screening, intelligence matters and K9 operations at international airports.
"We are putting all these measures in place and the public will see them being implemented at airports," he said.
Meanwhile, the value of seizures and government revenue leakages foiled by MCBA has exceeded RM265 million so far this year, nearly triple the RM80 million recorded last year.
Shuhaily said e-waste and drug smuggling were among the main contributors to the figure.
He attributed the increase to strengthened enforcement, including new schemes and efforts to foster a stronger work culture among its personnel.
He said the measures would continue to be strengthened to tighten controls at the country's entry points and curb smuggling and revenue leakages.
Also present at the event were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid and Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC probes UiTM Holdings over 2023 losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has launched an investigation into UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd over losses incurred by the company in 2023.
The commission said the investigation covers several issues, including the development of a 50-megawatt solar project in Gambang, Pahang, for which a payment of RM42 million was reportedly made without the approval of the board of directors.
"The investigation is still ongoing due to the complexity of the case, which involves technical aspects, and is awaiting further instructions from the prosecution.
"To complete the investigation, MACC will also examine whether there are other relevant issues, including governance weaknesses, as highlighted by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim," MACC said in a statement today.
It said it welcomed the prime minister's concern and firm stance in addressing the weaknesses that contributed to the losses suffered by UiTM Holdings.
Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed that the investigation is being conducted under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.
He said MACC would complete the investigation swiftly, independently and fairly.
Yesterday, Anwar had directed Universiti Teknologi Mara to
review UiTM Holdings' governance and management
over concerns about the company's losses.
He had said the review should be conducted in cooperation with the UiTM vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister's Department, which would provide support where necessary.
He was responding to an audience member who wanted the government and the UiTM Malaysia Alumni Federation to review the management of UiTM Holdings, which the student claimed had recorded losses of more than RM100 million.
The issue was raised during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM in Shah Alam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCBA needs world-class training academy - Chief Secretary
Article:
SEGAMAT: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) needs its own world-class training academy to produce highly skilled officers in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
He said developing in-house capabilities was crucial to ensuring that MCBA was prepared to face increasingly complex border security challenges and had the capacity to operate independently over the next 10 to 20 years.
"The world-class MCBA Training Academy is important for producing more talented and highly skilled Malaysians in border management technologies, including artificial intelligence, who are future-ready, uphold integrity and are committed to safeguarding national interests," he said at the passing-out ceremony for the MCBA Basic Training Course Series 1/2026 at the Segamat Police Training Centre (Pulapol) today.
Also present was MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Shamsul Azri said the proposed academy was in line with MCBA's plans to move beyond a reactive approach focused on securing the country's entry points towards smart, integrated and intelligence-led border control.
He said MCBA, currently in its first phase as 'Guardians of Checkpoint', must go beyond simply controlling the movement of people and goods at border entry points and shift from a reactive to a proactive approach.
"This is the change we must make – from guarding checkpoints to managing the border through smart, integrated and intelligence-led control, ultimately becoming the security leader for the country's entire border ecosystem," he said.
He said the development of MCBA's human capital must keep pace with technological advances and ever-evolving criminal modus operandi.
Shamsul Azri said officers' training should not end at the training centre but continue through on-the-job training, exposure to real operational situations and mentoring by experienced officers.
He said MCBA had also made encouraging progress in the approximately 23 months since its establishment, despite currently operating with only about 30 per cent of its optimum staffing level of 13,721 personnel.
He said the value of seizures and leakages prevented by MCBA this year had reached RM265 million, about three times the amount recorded in 2025.
Shamsul Azri also expressed his appreciation for MCBA's success in sending 436 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) back to their countries of origin through collaboration with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, police, Department of Environment and port authorities.
Meanwhile, he said the 408 pioneer MCBA officers who completed their three-month basic training today were the first batch to enter the public service under the new MCBA scheme, which came into effect on July 1.
They comprise 39 Penolong Penguasa Sempadan (Grade KS5) and 369 Pembantu Penguasa Sempadan (Grade KS1), who will be stationed at the Johor Baru-Singapore RTS Link entry point from Oct 1 in preparation for the full operation of the service on Jan 1, 2027. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FBM KLCI futures set for bargain hunting on US-China trade truce extension
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) futures contract is expected to attract bargain-hunting interest next week, supported by the extension of the US-China trade truce by another two months.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan said the extension reduces the immediate risk of another round of tariff escalation before year-end and provides greater visibility for businesses and supply chains.
"Improved risk appetite following the extension of the trade truce could provide room for the index to rebound, although elevated oil prices and global bond yields remain key downside risks.
The index is also trading closer to its recent year-to-date low of 1,656.83, which could encourage selective bargain hunting in fundamentally strong large-cap counters following the recent pullback," he said in his daily market update on WhatsApp Channels.
However, Mohd Sedek reckons that any near-term recovery is likely to remain selective rather than broad-based, as investors continue to monitor global bond yields, oil prices and foreign fund flows.
The FBM KLCI futures ended lower this week, tracking the weaker underlying cash market.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the September 2026 contract gained 18.5 points to 1,661.5, while the October 2026 and March 2027 contracts both gained 12.5 points to 1,655.0 and 1,647.5, respectively. The December 2026 note added 14.5 points to 1,664.0.
Weekly turnover surged to 145,235 lots from 27,714 lots last week, while open interest spiked to 145,426 contracts on Friday from 48,164 contracts a week earlier.
Over the last week, the FBM KLCI increased 6.06 points to settle at 1,671.62 yesterday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China, US agree to US$30bil tariff cut, AI dialogue during Xi visit
Article:
SHANGHAI: China said on Saturday it had agreed with the US on a US$30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement and on launching a dialogue on AI, under an eight-point consensus reached during President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.
The two sides have also agreed to set up a trade council and extend the outcomes of earlier talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.
The agreement follows an earlier move by the world's two largest economies to extend by two months a trade truce that had been due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on ‌a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.
The three-day summit between Xi and President Donald Trump, which ended on Friday, showcased personal diplomacy rather than big public breakthroughs. Xi has since landed in Beijing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday.
On artificial intelligence, the two sides agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology's risks and benefits, with the next round of discussions set for November, and to set up a communication channel for AI-related incidents, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.
Beyond the economy, they also agreed to support each other in hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting and the Group of 20 summit, with both leaders planning to attend the gatherings hosted by the other, as Trump had earlier said in a social media post.
On foreign policy, the leaders agreed that Iran should fulfil its commitment not to develop nuclear weapons and that no country or entity should impose transit tolls on international waterways, the ministry said.
The US Embassy in Beijing did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan businesswoman's RM500,000 Jeep among 3,790 luxury vehicles seized
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Jeep Wrangler worth nearly RM500,000 belonging to a popular Kelantan businesswoman was among 3,790 luxury vehicles seized by the Road Transport Department nationwide under Op Luxury.
Its senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the vehicle was seized in Jalan Taman Tengku Anis here at about 2.50pm on Sept 24.
He added that the jeep was seized after it was found to have an expired motor vehicle licence.
He said the 3,790 vehicles were seized between June 2025 and Sept 26 this year, with an estimated value of RM550 million.
"The operation is a continuation of Op Luxury, which has been carried out since last year to tackle serious offences involving luxury vehicle owners.
"Among the main offences detected are failure to renew road tax and insurance, driving without a valid licence and other offences," he told a press conference here today.
Of the total, Kifli said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December last year, while another 3,005 were seized from Jan 1 to Sept 26 this year.
"Negri Sembilan recorded the highest number of seizures with 469 vehicles, followed by Selangor (410), Kuala Lumpur (382), Johor (367) and Penang (357)," he added.
[[nid:1542252]]
He said enforcement was intensified after the department found that some luxury vehicle owners had failed to renew their road tax for years.
He said the most common reason given by owners was that they were reluctant to renew their road tax because their vehicles had been blacklisted due to previous offences or outstanding summonses.
"Some claimed they had previous offences, such as failing to comply with speed limits, or other outstanding summonses.
"What shocked us was that even lower-income vehicle owners were able to renew their road tax, while some luxury vehicle owners, who are generally from the T20 group, had failed to do so," he said.
He said the department had found cases where road tax had not been renewed for many years, including records dating back to 2014 and 2020.
Kifli said the vehicles seized ranged from supercars worth more than RM1 million, with the most expensive valued at RM8.8 million, to luxury vehicles worth between RM250,000 and RM1 million.
He said the number of supercars involved had declined, while vehicles in the RM250,000 to RM1 million range, including BMWs, Toyota Alphards and Toyota Vellfires, remained common.
He said more than 20 per cent of the 3,790 vehicles seized were linked to owners categorised as T20 based on the department's investigations and various indicators.
He said the group included entrepreneurs, particularly those in the cosmetics business, traders and influencers.
Kifli also said the department had detected cases involving owners of two or three vehicles using the same registration number, which resulted in additional offences being recorded.
He said the enforcement action had also contributed to government revenue, with the department collecting about RM35 million last year from summons payments and motor vehicle licence-related payments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Beyond the F1 circuit, Bagan Lalang offers a slower side of Sepang
Article:
WHILE thousands of motorsport fans will descend on Sepang for the Formula 1 action, there is another side of the district where the pace is considerably slower - one measured by sunsets, fishing boats and the ebb and flow of the tide.
At Pantai Bagan Lalang, just about 30 minutes away from the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), the sound of waves replaces roaring engines as campers pitch their tents along the coast, drawn by the beach's open views and its location at the meeting point of the sea and river.
As evening approaches, the sky over the Malacca Strait shifts into vibrant shades of orange, pink, and purple, making it a premier spot for sunset watchers.
For Chef Yang, 56, who has lived in Sepang since 2000, the beach has become a regular camping ground over the past five years.
"I camp almost every day," she said, adding that she preferred Bagan Lalang because of its location at the estuary, where she can watch the sunset and observe fishing boats coming and going.
"Here, you can see the fishermen heading out and returning at around 3am or 4am. You can see them lined up as they leave. This beach has its own uniqueness."
A retired chef who now organises events and develops recipes and camping modules, Chef Yang often camps alone, although she said the nature of camping meant she rarely remained a stranger for long.
"Even if you come alone, God will send people your way. Friends you don't know will arrive and become friends," she said, adding that Pantai Bagan Lalang is usually full of campers during the weekends and public holidays.
Her connection with the outdoors has also shaped how she spends her time at Bagan Lalang.
While the beach is not suitable for swimming, visitors can take part in activities such as night crab spotting, fishing and looking for oysters.
She and a friend also regularly clear rubbish and debris from the area, particularly as some campers may not realise that fallen wood and other material should not simply be burned.
The beach also attracts groups of motorhome owners, who make it a regular weekend destination, often arriving on Fridays and staying until Sunday.
Mohd Azmi Suito, 60, is another regular camper who prefers the freedom of deciding where to go and pitching his tent wherever he finds a place that feels right.
"I usually go wherever I feel like going. Wherever I stop, that's where I camp," he said.
For him, the sea offers a sense of calm, while camping in a natural setting allows him to meet fellow campers and exchange stories.
"I don't like complicated places. I prefer somewhere natural like this. When you meet people, they share stories and you forget, for a while, about the things you're going through," he said.
He said he also appreciated the quiet atmosphere at Pantai Bagan Lalang and would sometimes stay longer when he found the surroundings particularly peaceful.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chairman: 'UiTM Holdings has recovery plan to address losses'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd already has a recovery plan and proposals to address its financial position following accumulated losses of RM157 million, said its chairman Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya.
He said the recovery plan and proposals had been presented several times through governance channels, including to the university's Board of Directors.
"What is needed now is alignment, decision-making and implementation across the entire UiTM ecosystem," he said in a post on Facebook yesterday.
Fathul Bari said he acknowledged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's concerns over the losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Group.
"I appreciate the concern and firmness shown by the prime minister. This attention should serve as momentum to strengthen the recovery process already underway.
"However, the facts need to be placed within their proper timeline. The losses being referred to are not new losses incurred under the current leadership.
"The figure of RM157 million has been reported since 2023 and the Higher Education Ministry at the time explained that it represented accumulated losses dating back to 2007.
"The issue was also examined in the 2022 Auditor General's Report and through Public Accounts Committee (PAC) proceedings, followed by the tabling of the PAC report in 2024.
"These are the chronological facts. This is a legacy issue."
He said the past losses had created a trust deficit in UiTM Holdings.
"But a trust deficit should not be passed on indefinitely to a new leadership. The leadership has since changed, while governance is being strengthened. Therefore, the performance of the current leadership should be assessed based on its integrity, implementation and results."
He said the new leadership was determined to restore performance, strengthen governance, rebuild confidence and put UiTM Holdings back on a growth trajectory.
"We are not using legacy issues as an excuse. We are identifying those legacy issues in order to resolve them."
He also hoped that the issue would not be politicised by any party.
"This is not a political issue. This is about restoring an asset owned by the university. If UiTM Holdings is strengthened, the value will ultimately return to UiTM. If it remains weak, UiTM will also bear the consequences."
In the post, Fathul Bari also proposed that the prime minister, particularly in his capacity as finance minister, consider a national framework under which university holding companies and subsidiaries would be given a First Right of Refusal for suitable business opportunities within their respective university ecosystems, subject fully to merit, due diligence, competitiveness and good governance.
"This is not about free projects, nor is it about monopolies. It is about having the first opportunity to compete and be assessed professionally.
"If university companies are capable of undertaking such opportunities competitively, it would be more strategic for the economic value generated to remain within the university ecosystem.
"The profits of university subsidiaries should ultimately be channelled back towards strengthening the university."
Yesterday, Anwar directed Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to
review UiTM Holdings' governance and management
over concerns about the company's losses.
Anwar said the review should be conducted in cooperation with the UiTM vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister's Department, which would provide support where necessary.
The issue was raised during a question-and-answer session at the Himpunan Mesra Alumni UiTM at the Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor, UiTM, here.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Signalling disruption causes up to 5-hour delays for KTM Komuter, ETS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A signalling system disruption between Kalumpang and Kuala Kubu Baru yesterday left KTM Komuter and ETS services delayed by up to five hours.
In a statement today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) said KTM Komuter's worst delay hit Train No. 2389 at 230 minutes, while ETS service EP9138 (KL Sentral–Butterworth) had a 305-minute delay.
KTMB said preliminary checks traced the disruption to damage in a system component, which sparked and disrupted the signalling system.
The cause of the component damage, however, is still under further investigation.
"The signalling system disruption had a knock-on effect on the movement and schedules of other trains passing through the sector, particularly services to and from the north," the statement read.
Meanwhile, KTMB said the Rawang–Ipoh Double Tracking upgrade works, scheduled earlier, are also being carried out in stages, including along the Kalumpang route yesterday and today, requiring schedule adjustments on the affected line.
"The signalling disruption during those works further restricted train movements, compounding delays to several KTM Komuter and ETS services," the statement read.
However, KTMB said repair works were completed at 5.15am today, and the first Komuter train from Tanjung Malim departed at 5.45am.
The national rail operator said KTM Komuter and ETS services have now returned to normal, though a 30-minute delay from the original schedule persists due to the signalling fault along the Batang Kali route.
KTMB apologised to affected passengers for the incident, adding that full fare refunds will be given to those who chose not to continue their journey following the disruption, subject to prevailing procedures.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sepang businesses eye F1 windfall as race returns after nine years
Article:
THE roar of Formula 1 (F1) cars will return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, but for residents and businesses in the district, the race for economic gains may begin well before the chequered flag falls.
When the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix takes place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2-4, thousands of motorsport fans, racing teams and international visitors are expected to descend on the district.
Sepang member of parliament Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu said the race's return was expected to generate significant economic spillover for Sepang and surrounding areas, particularly in tourism, hospitality, transport, food and beverage, and small businesses.
"An international event of this scale has the potential to generate significant economic value of hundreds of millions, with the benefits extending not only to major industries but also to ordinary people who depend on daily business activities.
"The multiplier effect is expected to be felt through increased demand for hotels, homestays, rental apartments, transport services, restaurants, food stalls and various supporting businesses," she told the New Straits Times.
The ripple effect, she said, could extend beyond Sepang to Cyberjaya, Putrajaya and the wider Klang Valley as visitors look for places to stay, eat and explore.
She said this was also in line with the momentum of Visit Malaysia 2026, which aims to increase international tourist arrivals.
"F1 is not merely a racing event, but a platform to promote Malaysia, particularly Sepang, as a world-class tourism destination," she said.
The aim, she added, was to encourage visitors to stay longer, spend locally and discover the district beyond its famous racing circuit.
Sepang's attractions include Bagan Lalang's coastline, Sungai Pelek's agricultural offerings, mangrove ecosystems along the Sepang River and the Mah Meri Orang Asli community, alongside traditional villages and community-based tourism offerings.
Aiman Athirah said supporting programmes such as carnivals, cultural activities and tourism promotions could encourage visitors to extend their stays and spend in surrounding areas.
"Most importantly, these economic benefits must reach the people. We want small businesses, food-stall operators, local restaurants, homestay operators, e-hailing drivers, handicraft entrepreneurs and the service sector to also benefit from this historic event," she said.
[[nid:1542345]]
A Dragon Fruit Economy
One of Sepang's biggest local stories, however, is its dragon fruit fields.
The drive from SIC towards Bagan Lalang offers a glimpse of an agricultural economy that has become closely associated with the district, with dragon fruit stalls and farms lining the roads.
Pitaya cultivation in Sepang now covers 480 hectares and involves 265 farmers, with annual production estimated at 12,000 tonnes.
Aiman Athirah said the 2023 Agriculture Census showed Sepang was Malaysia's largest dragon fruit-producing district, recording 18,779.8 tonnes of production - ahead of other major producing districts such as Batu Pahat and Kluang.
The district also recorded the country's highest sales volume, at 15,047.1 tonnes.
"This shows that dragon fruit is no longer merely a side crop or small-scale farm produce.
"It has become an economic activity with commercial value and significant potential to be developed as a local agro-industry," she said.
For Aiman Athirah, that is exactly the kind of story Sepang should be able to tell when the world arrives for Formula 1.
"We do not want visitors to come to Sepang only because of F1, Kuala Lumpur International Airport or its beaches. We want them to know Sepang through its produce, food, farms and the communities behind them.
"F1 brings the world to Sepang. Dragon fruit, meanwhile, can bring Sepang's story to the world," she said.
More Than A Race
Aiman Athirah hopes the return of Formula 1 will also mark a new chapter for Malaysia on the global motorsport stage.
F1, she said, could help strengthen Malaysia's international image, attract high-quality tourists, create economic opportunities, promote technology and engineering, and inspire the younger generation.
"We want this event to leave a bigger legacy for the people, not just be an event lasting a few days, but become a catalyst for Sepang's economic development and global brand.
"We want that when the chequered flag is raised in Sepang, the world will see not just a race, but a Malaysia that is ready, progressive and capable of becoming a world-class host," she said.
Aiman Athirah said the government is also taking a comprehensive and coordinated approach to ensure the event runs smoothly and safely.
Preparations extend beyond SIC to the wider event ecosystem, including road infrastructure, traffic management, security and emergency response, cleanliness, public facilities and visitor management.
They also cover community participation and the readiness of Sepang's tourism and local economic sectors, with efforts aimed at ensuring the benefits of the event extend beyond the circuit itself.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Once Parliament is dissolved, we are no longer with them' - Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "The moment Parliament is dissolved, we are no longer with them."
That was the assurance from Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on the coalition's commitment to the unity government, which he said would end when the 15th Parliament is dissolved.
Zahid said BN had decided to join the unity government after the 15th general election (GE15) and would honour that commitment until the end of the parliamentary term.
"In this complex situation, we need one fixed compass. After GE15, Barisan Nasional decided to be part of the government, and our commitment is to remain in the government until the end of the 15th Parliament.
"The moment Parliament is dissolved, we are no longer with them. This is our promise," he said in his keynote address at the 18th Annual General Assembly of Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.
Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister and Umno president, said the commitment was a promise made to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and formalised through the formation of the unity government.
"Our promise to His Majesty the Y.ang di-Pertuan Agong, this is our promise. And this is the promise we made in the formation of the Malaysian unity government," he said.
However, Zahid said BN's participation in the government did not mean it had surrendered its identity or its own political position.
"Cooperation in the government does not mean Barisan Nasional has surrendered its identity or stopped having its own position," he said.
He said political arrangements at the federal and state levels could differ, citing Johor as an example of BN contesting independently at state level despite its participation in the federal government.
Makkal Sakti president Datuk Seri R.S. Thanenthiran, meanwhile, urged BN to leave the unity government as soon as possible, saying the coalition and its leaders had been repeatedly pressured and tested.
He said the party wanted the matter to be brought to the BN leadership at the highest level for discussion through a resolution passed at its 18th annual general assembly today.
"Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia proposes that Barisan Nasional leave the Madani Government as soon as possible," he said in his policy speech.
Thanenthiran alleged that Umno and BN leaders had been repeatedly subjected to pressure, including arrests and investigations, while claiming that similar action had not been taken against politicians on the other side.
"It is as though this Madani party, this Madani government, is trying to pressure Barisan Nasional and its leaders into surrendering," he said.
He said Makkal Sakti wanted the resolution to be taken to the BN leadership for consideration, stressing that the party had had enough of its leaders being subjected to pressure.
"Once again, the party urges that this resolution be brought to the Barisan leadership at the highest level for discussion.
"Enough is enough. We have been tested enough. Our leaders have been tested enough," he said.
He also warned that BN's continued participation in the unity government could affect the coalition's reputation.
"As long as Barisan Nasional remains in the Madani Government, its name will also be tainted," he said.
Thanenthiran said Makkal Sakti wanted to act as a "benteng", or bulwark, for BN and would stand with the coalition and its leaders when they came under pressure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JPJ seizes 3,790 luxury vehicles worth RM550m in nationwide crackdown since June 2025
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — A total of 3,790 luxury vehicles worth an estimated RM550 million were seized by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) under Ops Luxury from June 2025 to yesterday for various offences.
JPJ senior director of enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said 785 vehicles were seized between June and December 2025, while another 3,005 were seized from January to September 26 this year.
He said Negeri Sembilan recorded the highest number of seizures with 469 vehicles, followed by Selangor (410), Kuala Lumpur (382), Johor (367) and Penang (357).
“Some luxury vehicle owners said they were reluctant to go to JPJ offices to renew their road tax because they had been blacklisted for previous offences.
“What is puzzling is that lower-income groups can come forward to renew their road tax, while owners of luxury vehicles from the T20 group give various reasons for not doing so, resulting in their vehicles being seized,” he told a press conference at the Panji JPJ Office here today.
He said investigations found that an estimated 20 per cent of the luxury vehicle owners were cosmetic entrepreneurs, influencers and businesspeople.
Muhammad Kifli said JPJ would continue Ops Luxury to ensure that all road users comply with the law, regardless of the price or type of vehicle or the status of its owner.
“Being able to afford a luxury vehicle comes with the responsibility to comply with the law. Owners and drivers are responsible for ensuring that all vehicle and driving documents remain valid, and that their vehicles meet all requirements before being driven on the road,” he said. — Bernama

Title: A month without answers: Families of missing Malaysians told Nepal search may soon end
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 27 — After more than a month of waiting without news, the families of Malaysians still missing following the flood disaster in Nepal are beginning to resign themselves to all possibilities when informed that the government of that country is considering ending the search and rescue (SAR) operations.
In a meeting with government agencies at Wisma Putra today, the next of kin were also briefed on the process related to the death certificates, which are being expedited to facilitate the families’ affairs.
S. Sankara, the son of a missing Malaysian, said Wisma Putra informed them that the Nepalese government is expected to conclude the rescue operation phase soon before transitioning to recovery operations.
“Based on the briefing received, the search and rescue operation is still ongoing at this time. The family was briefed on the documentation process, including the death certificate that will be issued by the Nepalese government,” he said to the media when met at the Wisma Putra compound here today.
The four-hour meeting, which started around 10.15 am and ended around 3 pm, involved briefings from several agencies regarding SAR operations, management of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples, as well as legal and documentation processes.
Meanwhile, Sankara said his family is trying to continue with their lives as best as they can despite still facing emotional pressure following the loss of his mother, K. Kalaimathi, 57, who was in Nepal for a religious ritual.
For Adura Masood, the wait for her husband, Dr. Mohd Padzil Daros, 63, is still not over.
“Not yet. No news,” she said when asked about any update on her husband.
Adura said today’s briefing explained the search efforts carried out by the involved teams, but there has not been much new development regarding the victim’s whereabouts.
“I don’t think there has been much (development). They explained what happened there, just a brief explanation. It’s just a briefing,” she said.
However, Adura believes that the team involved has done their best in the search effort.
“I think they have done their job,” she said.
Mohd Padzil was among the members of a group known as “Team Loe” who were reported missing when they were about 18 kilometres from the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border.
The group was reported to be travelling from Kathmandu to the Nepal-Tibet border in a four-wheel-drive vehicle when the disaster struck the Rasuwa area.
Among those who participated in the journey were members of the special team from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, and JBPM Fire and Rescue Operations Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul.
Also participating in the same mission were Ganesh Neupane, Shabuddin Mun, Azman Karim, Muhammad Hazig Ismail, Mohd Nohan Salim, Jason Ngeow and Muhamad Nasir Abdul Talib.
Today’s meeting is the second following the government’s first official engagement with the affected families on Aug 30, five days after the incident on Aug 26, but not all families were represented at that time.
Among those involved are representatives from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Department of Chemistry, the National Registration Department (JPN), the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, and the Department of Social Welfare (JKM).
The flood and debris flow on August 26, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche in the upper Lhende Khola watershed in Tibet, and reportedly claimed more than 1,450 lives, while thousands more remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: Dr Wan Azizah wants women to make up at least 30pc of PKR candidates in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 27 — The principle of justice must continue to be the cornerstone of PKR’s struggle as it faces the Melaka state election, said the party’s Advisory Council chairman Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
She said the party’s struggle was not merely about gaining power, but about ensuring that every Malaysian received the justice they deserved.
“We want every Malaysian to have justice. That is what we uphold in our party and in our struggle,” she told reporters after launching the Melaka Wanita PKR election machinery here today.
Also present were prime minister’s political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin and Melaka Wanita PKR chief Mahani Masban.
Dr Wan Azizah, who is also Bandar Tun Razak MP said PKR members must remain steadfast in upholding the principle despite various challenges, including the departure of some members from the party.
She said PKR’s long experience had shown that change did not come easily, but required sustained effort and commitment from party members.
Dr Wan Azizah urged Melaka Wanita PKR to play an important role in garnering voters’ support and strengthening the party’s spirit of struggle at the grassroots level.
She also expressed hope that Wanita PKR would be given the opportunity to contest in the state election, with women making up at least 30 per cent of the total candidates.
Meanwhile, Azman said PKR could spring a surprise in Melaka if it had a disciplined, well-trained and committed election machinery.
He said the party’s machinery needed to work harder, given that PKR currently held no seats in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly. — Bernama

Title: Calls unanswered, woman forces entry and finds fiancé dead in Melaka home
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 27 — A woman was left heartbroken after finding her fiancé lying lifeless in his home, having failed to reach him since last night.
The 38-year-old went to his house in Simpang Ampat around 11am today after growing anxious when her calls went unanswered,
Harian Metro
(HM) reported.
Alor Gajah district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said she had gone to the man’s residence to look for him after being unable to contact him.
“On arriving, she entered the house through a window and found him inside the unit before calling for an ambulance. Further checks confirmed he had died,” he told HM.
The victim, who worked at a factory, is believed to have been living alone at the property.

Title: MetMalaysia alerts seven states to evening thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in parts of seven states until 7pm today.
In Perak, the affected area is Hulu Perak, while in Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang and Pasir Puteh, MetMalaysia said in a statement.
The warning also covers Besut, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman, Marang and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Pekan, Rompin and Jerantut in Pahang; and Kota Tinggi and Mersing in Johor.
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Kapit, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Bintulu, Miri, Limbang, Samarahan, Serian, Kuching and Sri Aman (Lubok Antu).
